messages:
sanjay r: Quick heads-up — I'm prototyping a routing + telemetry pattern that maps org API keys to a lightweight tenant billing label and sampled telemetry tag. Goal: keep console dashboards low-cardinality while preserving per-tenant SLA/quotas for billing and alerting. WIP doc: https://go/redwood/ops/tenant-key-mapper (draft).

ingrid c: Do you mean the mapping lives in the control plane or at the edge gateway? major difference for latency and PII exposure.

sanjay r: Control plane doing the canonical mapping. Edge receives a derived tag (tenant_label) and sampling bucket. No raw org_id forwarded in telemetry; only hashed id for debug traces if needed.

claire w: +1 on derived tag. We should also avoid sending billing_tier in every event — that creates duplication. Send tenant_label + sampling_bucket, resolve billing_tier in the console backend when aggregating.

ben t: How does quota enforcement work then? We still need per-org hard limits, throttles, and accurate billing counters. If edge only has tenant_label, how do we ensure enforcement correctness?

sanjay r: Enforcement stays at the gateway using cached mapping (TTL 5m). Gateway enforces based on mapped quota bucket id. Control plane periodically pushes mapping diffs. Fallback: if mapping missing, gateway rejects with 429 + code SUBSCRIPTION_PENDING.

tariq k: What about rollout UX in console? Products will want to see migration progress: how many keys moved to new billing labels, errors, rejected requests. We need dashboard tiles for that.

ingrid c: dashboard idea: per-key migration table with columns: key, previous_plan, resolved_label, last_seen, sample_rate, rejection_count. But we must keep sampling so that per-tenant request traces don't explode.

sanjay r: Example routing policy snippet (proto YAML):

```yaml
# routing-policy snippet (for prototype)
mappings:
  - org_key_prefix: "org_abc"
    tenant_label: "team-pulse-standard"
    quota_bucket: "q-std-100k"
    sample_rate: 0.001  # 0.1% telemetry sampling
  - org_key_prefix: "org_xyz"
    tenant_label: "team-labs-prem"
    quota_bucket: "q-prem-unlimited"
    sample_rate: 0.01   # 1% telemetry sampling
```

and a sample telemetry event that edge emits (no PII):

```text
ts=3167896543 event=request.latency_ms route=/v1/generate tenant_label=team-pulse-standard sample_bucket=37 latency_ms=120
```

claire w: Nice. Two questions: 1) how do we pick sample_bucket (deterministic hashing of org_key so we get stable sampling), and 2) are we comfortable with the 5m mapping TTL for quota changes (e.g., immediate customer suspend)?

sanjay r: sample_bucket = fnv64(org_key) % 1000 (deterministic). For immediate suspends we send a control-plane push to gateway (webhook/push-stream) which can invalidate cache immediately. The TTL is a safety-net.

ben t: For billing counters we need exact counts — so sampled telemetry can't be used for billing. We'll keep synchronous billing counters in gateway to a durable counter (summary increment). Telemetry is only for dashboards/quality/alerting.

claire w: Agreed. That separation addresses cardinality vs accuracy. We'll also add a telemetry flag: "telemetry_mode=light|debug" so we can enable denser traces for flagged tenants.

tariq k: Rollout plan suggestion: stage 1 (1% of keys) — observe dashboard mutation heat; stage 2 (10%) — push canary mapping; stage 3 — global. Console should show a rollout widget with toggle + current % + failback button. Also surface per-key rejection samples.

ingrid c: Privacy check: logging only hashed key + tenant_label. Need security sign-off to ensure hashed key isn't considered PII in our regions.

sanjay r: noted, I'll file a short PR to security and legal.

ben t: I'll own the gateway counter integration and can run the 1% canary next week.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment started for tenant-mapping v1 -> canary group 1 (1% keys) at 3167896590.

sanjay r: Thanks — action items: (1) security review (sanjay), (2) gateway counter integration (ben), (3) console rollout widget mockups (tariq + claire), (4) control-plane push API spec (ingrid). I'll update the doc with the snippets above and a sketch of the dashboard metrics.

ingrid c: ok, will draft the push API spec by Friday.

claire w: I'll mock the rollout tile and migration table tomorrow.

sanjay r: great, leaving notes in the doc. If anyone has objections to the privacy-preserving mapping approach, speak up here. Otherwise we'll start canary tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
